datasets.variant_notes: 7 subjects (Prealgebra, Algebra, Number Theory, Counting and Probability, Geometry, Intermediate Algebra, Precalculus) with 5 difficulty levels each
datasets.annotation_method: Problems collected from US mathematics competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, etc.) via aops.com; solutions written in LaTeX with step-by-step derivations

data_creator_info.creator_type: competition organizers (original problems) + paper authors (curation, formatting)
data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: UC Berkeley, UChicago; problems sourced from Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) community
data_creator_info.evidence: problems from mathematics competitions including the AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more. Many of these problems can be collected from aops.com/community/c3158_usa_contests

datasets.notes: 12,500 problems total (7,500 training, 5,000 test). Problems tagged by difficulty 1-5. Answers normalized for exact-match evaluation using \boxed{} delimiter. Problems and solutions formatted in LaTeX with Asymptote vector graphics language for figures.

datasets.variant_notes: Two subsets: Khan Academy (~100,000 problems) and Mathematica (~5 million problems)
datasets.annotation_method: Khan Academy problems pulled from Khan Academy exercises (github.com/Khan/khan-exercises); Mathematica problems generated from 100 hand-designed scripts (37 with step-by-step solutions)

data_creator_info.creator_type: Khan Academy (existing exercises) + paper authors (Mathematica scripts)
data_creator_info.evidence: Khan Academy subset has 693 exercise types with over 100,000 problems and full solutions... we also contribute our own Mathematica scripts to generate approximately 50x more problems

datasets.notes: 23 GB total. Khan Academy covers elementary math to multivariable calculus. Mathematica covers algebra, calculus, counting, statistics, geometry, linear algebra, number theory. Designed as auxiliary pretraining dataset for MATH.
